# shadow/no-unsafe-spread-user-input

Disallow spreading untrusted data onto DOM elements.

`recommended`

## Why

`<div {...obj} />` copies every key of `obj` onto the element: `on*` handlers, `href`, `style`, `innerHTML`. If `obj` comes from the URL, a form or parsed JSON, whoever controls it controls the element. Copy the keys you expect (`pick`, or explicit attributes) instead of spreading everything.

## Incorrect

```tsx
<div {...JSON.parse(text)} />
```

```tsx
<input {...Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form))} />
```

```tsx
<a {...searchParams} />
```

```tsx
const attrs = JSON.parse(raw);
const view = <div {...attrs} />;
```

## Correct

```tsx
<div {...props} />
```

```tsx
<div {...pick(JSON.parse(text), ['id', 'title'])} />
```

```tsx
<Widget {...JSON.parse(text)} />
```

## Options

```json
[
  {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "sources": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "sanitizers": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
]
```

Defaults: `[{}]`

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/no-unsafe-spread-user-input`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/no-unsafe-spread-user-input */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/no-unsafe-spread-user-input */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. When the data only looks untrusted, for example a `payload` your own code built from fixed keys. When a function of yours restricts the keys, list it in `sanitizers` instead.

## Notes

- Only DOM elements (lower-case tags) are checked: a component decides for itself what to do with its props.
- Sources: `JSON.parse`, `Object.fromEntries`, `useSearchParams`/`useParams`, `location.*`, `event.*`, `request.*`, and variables initialized from them. Option `sources` adds more dotted prefixes (regular expressions as strings) and calls.
- Option `sanitizers` (default `pick`, `allow`, `allowlist`, `allowAttributes`, `sanitizeProps`, `splitProps`) names functions that restrict the keys; a list given here replaces the default one.
- Followed through `?.`, `await` (in async components too), TypeScript wrappers, and either branch of `?:`, `||`, `??` and `&&`.

## Messages

- `unsafeSpread`: Spreading `{{source}}` onto <{{tag}}> lets untrusted data set any attribute, including `on*` handlers, `href` and `innerHTML`. Copy the allowed keys explicitly.
